# A Speaker In The Debunking Calisthenics Myths Ep.7 Podcast Allows Bad Form For A Few Mesocycles With Gifted Athletes

A speaker in the podcast says that sometimes you can allow bad form in training, especially with gifted people, for a few mesocycles, and then reset. [src: vid-OYFU5AyLl9w]

## Details

- The speaker says that sometimes you can allow for bad form in training, especially when working with gifted people. [src: vid-OYFU5AyLl9w]
- The speaker gives gifted people a few mesocycles to push more, because the speaker knows they don't get hurt. [src: vid-OYFU5AyLl9w]
- After that they focus on improving the little details that still need improvement, do a lot of volume there, and then go back and improve the form. [src: vid-OYFU5AyLl9w]
- The speaker calls this an outlier scenario, not what you do. [src: vid-OYFU5AyLl9w]

## Evidence

- vid-OYFU5AyLl9w (not stated): "Sometimes you can allow for bad form in your training, especially when I'm working with gifted people, I will give them a few mesocycles to push more to see where they get. I know they don't get hurt."
- vid-OYFU5AyLl9w (not stated): "We focus on improving those little details that still need improvement, do a lot of volume there, and then go back and improve the form."
- vid-OYFU5AyLl9w (not stated): "But this is outlier scenario, not what you do."
